name: stri_split_charclass
title: Split a String By Pattern Matches

origin.description: Split each string on code points from a character class.
origin.usage: stri_split_charclass(str, pattern, n = -1L, omit_empty = FALSE, tokens_only = FALSE, simplify = FALSE)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to split.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Maximum number of pieces. Negative means every piece. Zero returns an empty vector. A positive n keeps n - 1 pieces and the remainder.

arguments.name: omit_empty
arguments.text: TRUE drops empty pieces. NA replaces them with NA.

arguments.name: tokens_only
arguments.text: If TRUE, a positive n keeps at most n whole pieces and drops the remainder.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: If TRUE, return a character matrix padded with empty strings. NA pads with NA. The width is at least the largest positive n.

origin.details: Delimiters are not kept. n at least 2147483646 is an error. A missing string, pattern, or n is a one-element NA vector.
origin.value: A list of character vectors, or a character matrix when simplify is not FALSE.
origin.example:
x <- stri_split_charclass("a b c", "\\p{Z}")[[1]]
sentence <- paste0('stri_split_charclass("a b c", "\\p{Z}") returns ', paste(x, collapse = ", "), '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Split each string on code points from a character class.
translation.usage: stri_split_charclass(str, pattern, n=-1, omit_empty=False, tokens_only=False, simplify=False)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error. Membership is ICU 76, Unicode 16.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Maximum number of pieces. Negative means every piece. Zero returns an empty list. A positive n keeps n - 1 pieces and the remainder.

arguments.name: omit_empty
arguments.text: True drops empty pieces. NA replaces them with NA.

arguments.name: tokens_only
arguments.text: If true, a positive n keeps at most n whole pieces and drops the remainder.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: If true, return a list of rows padded with empty strings. NA pads with NA. The width is at least the largest positive n.

translation.details: Delimiters are not kept. n at least 2147483646 is an error. A missing string, pattern, or n is a one-element NA list.
translation.value: A list of lists of strings, or a list of rows when simplify is not false.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_split_charclass
x = stri_split_charclass("a b c", "\\p{Z}")
sentence = f'stri_split_charclass("a b c", "\\p{{Z}}") returns {", ".join(x[0])}.'
print(sentence)
